evidence_gaps_add: No linked study prints measured peak host or GPU memory; Samarakoon et al. 2025 and Franzoso et al. 2025 show memory use only in figures.
No linked study repeats runs, so run-to-run variation of runtime or of variant calls is not measured; Samarakoon et al. 2025 compare Parabricks on two A100 clusters only in a figure.
No linked study reports accuracy in the same printed table as runtime; Samarakoon et al. 2025 show accuracy and CPU concordance in Figure 5 only.
No study of a genomic foundation model's inference runtime, memory or cost was found in this pass.
Costs are cloud list prices or authors' estimates at the time of each study and exclude storage and software licences unless stated.
evidence_gaps_keep: A separate ~2-hour joint-aggregation figure over 3,202 genomes at concurrency 200 is a different operation and is not assigned to this single-sample runtime.
use_case_changes.exclusions_note: The peak-memory exclusion stays: no source in this pass prints measured peak memory. The foundation-model exclusion text ('none is ingested in this bounded intake') remains true. No exclusion change is proposed.
use_case_changes.setting_proposed: Germline WGS and WES execution benchmarks on the same inputs: CPU-only GATK, Parabricks on L4, A100 and H100 GPUs and DRAGEN v4.2 on ten WGS samples (Samarakoon et al. 2025); six callers on CPU and 2, 4 and 8 GPU cloud and DGX machines on HG002 30x (O'Connell et al. 2023); Sentieon DNASeq and Parabricks Germline on cost-matched Google Cloud machines (Franzoso et al. 2025); plus the DRAGEN 4.2 developer runtime baseline on HG002.
use_case_changes.decision_proposed: Inspect per-sample wall-clock runtime and cost for the CPU, GPU and FPGA execution set-ups that match the team's hardware and sequencing type before budgeting a workflow; none of these is a foundation-model execution benchmark.
use_case_changes.output_proposed: Sourced per-sample runtime, cost, speedup and cost-saving values for exact pipeline, version and hardware configurations, with the limits of each comparison; no foundation-model execution benchmark and no clinical turnaround claim.
use_case_changes.pin_warning: Changing setting, decision or output alters fields pinned by the reviewed judgement use-case-mapping-amp-20261007-issue18, which would then be withheld until re-reviewed and re-pinned. Adding links, gaps, sources and citations does not.

summary_proposal.value: Three execution benchmarks are linked, alongside the existing DRAGEN developer baseline (HG002 full pipeline 1,838.5 seconds). None prints repeated runs, measured peak memory or accuracy next to runtime, and hardware differs within each comparison, so differences mix software and hardware. On ten WGS samples run by a University of Oslo group (Samarakoon et al. 2025), read mapping plus HaplotypeCaller for NA12878 (47.55x) took 2,317.7 minutes on a CPU-only GATK pipeline, 123.45 minutes with Parabricks on four L4 GPUs, 78.12 on four A100 GPUs, 54.22 on eight H100 GPUs and 60.29 on DRAGEN v4.2. On the same H100 machine, Parabricks DeepVariant took 14.58 minutes for NA12878 with version 4.1.0-1 and 16.05 with version 4.3.0-1. On one HG002 30x genome in the cloud (O'Connell et al. 2023; the authors' firm is an NVIDIA, AWS and Google alliance partner), HaplotypeCaller took 36.26 hours and cost 49.32 USD on a 32-vCPU AWS machine, and 0.59 hours and 17.5 USD on eight A100 GPUs on GCP. Some somatic callers cost more on GPUs: LoFreq cost 4.1 USD on the AWS CPU machine and 19 to 30.1 USD on GPU machines. On cost-matched Google Cloud machines (Franzoso et al. 2025), Sentieon DNASeq took 14 to 16 minutes per exome and 3:00 to 3:50 per genome, and Parabricks Germline on one T4 GPU 10 to 14 minutes and 4:06 to 4:40, at 0.71 to 1.03 USD per exome and 8.02 to 10.7 USD per genome, excluding the Sentieon licence; two genome runtime cells appear mis-entered and are left out of these ranges. No linked study measures the execution of a genomic foundation model.
